title: Joy Deficit — Life-Course Systems Map
subtitle: Childhood → Adolescence → Adulthood, across five ‘systemic layers’
centralUserNote: The map is centered on the “adult-in-formation”: the user is an ordinary adult who has succumbed to the unspoken pressures and rules set by the reward systems in place at the different stages of their life. The lens is that of a person whose work, identity, leisure, and self-promotion are unusually entangled.
approach: A chronologic approach treats growth and identity development as a sequence of age defined roles within reward systems, opportunities, constraints, and transitions, where earlier conditions shape later ones rather than appearing in isolation.
thesis: Across the life course, social systems increasingly reward visible performance, measurable achievement, and externally validated engagement; intrinsic joy—curiosity, voluntary play, absorption, experimentation, connection, and purposeless delight—receives less protected time, legitimacy, and infrastructure.
centralVisualClaim: Across the life course, systems increasingly convert play into preparation, performance, data, status, consumption, or recovery for work—while giving progressively less institutional protection to curiosity, direct connection, and purposeless joy.
designFraming: Creating conditions in which adults can access play without having to earn, quantify, display, optimize, or justify it.
designFramingNote: Position the potential design intervention not as “bringing back childishness.” This framing leaves room for an adult toy, social ritual, service, space, or critical artifact; the eventual intervention should emerge from the most consequential leverage point in the map. Do not select or rank an intervention node.
caveats: This map should not claim that all extrinsic rewards are harmful: Self-Determination Theory distinguishes controlling rewards from informational feedback, and identifies autonomy, competence, and relatedness as psychological needs that sustain self-motivation and wellbeing.
Evidence suggests expected, tangible, engagement-, completion-, and performance-contingent rewards can reduce later free-choice intrinsic motivation for already-interesting activities.
Do not label screen use as inherently deficient; distinguish self-directed, social, creative digital play from attention-extractive design.
International nodes are comparative references, not the map's central scope.
Age ranges overlap between adjacent substages and are informational only; layout must use substage order, not age.
